collection.descriptionHtml:
Water heaters and the parts that go around them: tank and tankless units in natural gas, propane and electric, heat pump models, plus pans, stands, straps, vent kits, gas supplies, connectors, dip tubes and anode rods. Brands include Rheem, Ruud, Navien, Noritz, Stiebel Eltron, Camco and Easyflex.

Efficiency splits the gas catalog in two. Atmospheric units vent by natural draft into a metal flue. Condensing units, at 90% efficiency and above, require sealed plastic or stainless venting plus a condensate drain, which is what turns a like-for-like swap into a bigger job. Check the vent path before ordering a high-efficiency replacement. Most water connections are 3/4" on residential tanks, with 1-1/2" and 2" on commercial models.

How to choose

  • Fuel. Stay with the fuel the building already has unless you are prepared to run a new gas line or a 240 V circuit.
  • Tank or tankless. A tank is sized by gallons and first-hour rating. A tankless unit is sized by flow in GPM at your winter temperature rise.
  • Venting. Atmospheric, power vent, direct vent and condensing models each need a different vent. Match the heater to the vent path the space allows.
  • Electrical supply. Residential electric tanks here run on 240 V with 4.5 or 5.5 kW elements. Heat pump models come in 240 V and 120 V plug-in versions. Whole-house electric tankless units need several 240 V breakers.
  • Installation parts. Plan for a drain pan, a relief valve discharge line, flexible connectors and, on a closed system, a thermal expansion tank.

Common questions

What size water heater do I need?

For a tank, compare the first-hour rating on the spec sheet with your busiest hour of hot water use. For a tankless unit, add up the flow of the fixtures that run at the same time and compare it with the unit's flow at your winter temperature rise.

Can a condensing water heater use my old vent?

No. Condensing units need sealed plastic or stainless venting and a condensate drain, so they cannot vent into an existing atmospheric flue. Follow the venting section of the installation manual for the model.

Do I need an expansion tank with a new water heater?

On a closed system, one with a check valve, backflow preventer or pressure reducing valve on the supply, heated water has nowhere to expand and the relief valve can drip. A potable thermal expansion tank on the cold inlet absorbs that volume. Local code decides whether one is required.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Tankless water heaters heat water only when a tap opens, so there is no storage tank to keep hot and no 40 or 50 gallon limit on a long shower. This collection brings together the complete tankless units listed in the store, in natural gas, propane and electric, from Navien, Rheem, Noritz and Stiebel Eltron. Valve kits, vent pipe and repair parts are listed separately.

Gas units for whole-house use run from 120,000 to 199,900 Btu/h. Propane models suit homes off the gas main, and the Navien NPE-2 and Rheem IKONIC units are field-convertible between the two fuels. Electric tankless heaters need no vent or gas line, but an 18 to 36 kW whole-house unit draws roughly 75 to 150 amps, so check your electrical panel first.

How to choose

  • Size by GPM, not gallons. Add up the flow of the fixtures that run at the same time, then check each unit's flow at your winter temperature rise. The 199,900 Btu/h Rheem gas units here are listed at 4.7 to 5.6 GPM at a 70°F rise. Colder groundwater means less flow from the same heater.
  • Fuel. Natural gas, propane or electric. Never run a natural gas unit on propane without the manufacturer's conversion.
  • Condensing or non-condensing. Condensing units here are listed at up to 0.96 UEF and vent through PVC, CPVC or polypropylene, with a condensate drain. Non-condensing units use the vent system named in their installation manual, such as the 3"/5" concentric vent on Rheem RTG indoor models.
  • Indoor or outdoor. Outdoor models need no vent pipe. Indoor models need a vent run planned with the heater.
  • Electric supply. Whole-house electric units need 240 V and several double-pole breakers. Small point-of-use models serve a single sink.

Common questions

What size tankless water heater do I need?

Add up the GPM of the fixtures that run at the same time and compare it with each unit's flow at your winter temperature rise. Our guide on what size tankless water heater you need walks through the math.

Is there a 120V tankless water heater?

Small point-of-use units run on 120 V and serve one sink. Whole-house electric units need 240 V. See point-of-use water heaters.

Can a tankless water heater use my old water heater vent?

No. Condensing units vent in PVC, CPVC or polypropylene, and non-condensing units use the vent system named in their installation manual. Neither vents into an existing atmospheric flue.

Related: gas tankless water heaters, electric tankless water heaters, propane tankless water heaters, Navien tankless water heaters and tankless valve kits.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Gas tankless water heaters from 120,000 to 199,900 Btu/h, in natural gas, propane and field-convertible versions, condensing and non-condensing, from Rheem, Navien and Noritz.

A tankless heater has no storage, so it is sized by flow at a given temperature rise, not by gallons. The same unit delivers less hot water where the incoming groundwater is colder, because the burner has a fixed maximum output. Size from your local winter inlet temperature and the fixtures that must run at once: two showers and a dishwasher call for a different unit than one bathroom. Check the gas supply before ordering.

How to choose

  • Input and flow. Add up the fixtures that run at the same time and check the unit's flow at your winter temperature rise. The 199,900 Btu/h Rheem condensing units here are listed at 5.5 to 5.6 GPM at a 70°F rise.
  • Condensing or non-condensing. A condensing unit vents in PVC, CPVC or polypropylene and needs a condensate drain with neutralization, since the condensate is acidic. Non-condensing units use the vent system named in their installation manual. Neither vents into an existing atmospheric flue.
  • Fuel. Some models are field-convertible with the manufacturer's kit, and others are sold as separate natural gas and propane versions. Check the fuel type in the product title.
  • Gas supply. Size the gas pipe to the full input and the length of the run, and confirm the meter can carry the load.
  • Recirculation. Models with a built-in recirculation pump, such as the Navien NPE-A2 and NHW700 AI and the Rheem IKONIC models with a recirculation pump, avoid a separate pump on a retrofit.

Common questions

What size gas tankless water heater do I need?

Size by flow and temperature rise, not by gallons. Add up the fixtures that will run at the same time and check the unit's flow at your winter temperature rise. See our guide to sizing a tankless water heater.

Condensing or non-condensing?

Condensing units vent in PVC, CPVC or polypropylene and need a condensate drain with a neutralizer. Non-condensing units use the vent system named in their installation manual. Neither can use an existing atmospheric flue.

Can I switch between natural gas and propane?

Some models are field-convertible with the manufacturer's kit, and others are sold as separate natural gas and propane versions. Check the fuel type in the product title before ordering.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Electric tankless water heaters from 8 kW through 36 kW at 240 V, from single-bath units to whole-house models, from Rheem and Stiebel Eltron.

Electrical capacity, not plumbing, decides whether these can be installed. The 27 kW model here is listed at 113 amps with three 40-amp breakers, and the 36 kW model at 150 amps with four. Electric tankless has no venting and no combustion air requirement, which is its advantage over gas in tight or interior spaces. Smaller 8 to 13 kW models suit a single bathroom or a warm-climate home; 24 to 36 kW models serve a whole house.

How to choose

  • kW and temperature rise. Sizing follows temperature rise, not gallons. The same unit delivers less hot water where the incoming groundwater is colder, because the element has a fixed kW output.
  • Panel capacity. Divide the kW rating by the voltage to get the amp draw, then check the breakers and wire size in the installation manual against your service.
  • Voltage. The whole-house models here are 240 V. A 120 V model only serves a single sink.
  • Fixtures served. Size from your local winter inlet temperature and the fixtures you need to run at the same time.

Common questions

What breakers does an electric tankless water heater need?

It depends on the kW rating. The 27 kW model here is listed with three 40-amp breakers and the 36 kW model with four. Check your panel before you order.

What size electric tankless heats a whole house?

24 to 36 kW models serve a whole house. 8 to 13 kW models suit one bathroom or a warm-climate home.

Is there a 120V electric tankless water heater?

Yes, for a single sink. Point-of-use units run on 120 V. See point-of-use water heaters.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Navien tankless water heaters heat water on demand, with no storage tank to keep hot. This page lists the complete Navien units in the store: the NPE-2 condensing series from the NPE-150S2 to the NPE-240S2 and NPE-240A2, rated up to 0.96 UEF, plus the mid-efficiency NHW700 and NPN lines. All are gas-fired, from 120,000 to 199,900 Btu/h.

The NPE-2 runs 0.93 to 0.96 UEF on dual stainless steel heat exchangers and vents through 2" or 3" PVC, CPVC or polypropylene. It is rated to 10,100 feet and certified to SCAQMD 1146.2 at under 20 ppm NOx. The NHW700 and NPN lines run 0.81 UEF with a stainless steel heat exchanger and are Ultra Low NOx. Choose the series first, then size by flow at your winter temperature rise. Venting kits, isolation valve kits and repair parts are listed separately.

How to choose

  • Read the model number for capacity. Navien numbers the NPE by nominal size, not by input: NPE-150S2 is 120,000 Btu/h, NPE-180 is 150,000, NPE-210 is 180,000 and NPE-240 is 199,900. Flow at a 67°F rise runs from 3.4 GPM on the 150 up to 5.8 GPM on the 240S2.
  • S2 or A2. The S2 is the base condensing unit at 0.93 to 0.96 UEF. The A2 is ComfortFlow: a built-in recirculation pump and buffer tank in the same cabinet, 0.95 UEF, and a minimum draw under 0.01 GPM against 0.5 GPM. On a retrofit the A2 removes the external pump and crossover valve.
  • Condensing or mid-efficiency. NHW-SU and NPN units are lighter and smaller than the NPE: 55 to 65 lbs and 14" wide against 62 to 77 lbs and 17.3" wide. The NHW700 AI models carry a built-in pump and buffer tank.
  • Location. The NHW-SU and NPN-U install indoors or outdoors, and the NPN-E is exterior only.
  • Gas and vent. Size the gas pipe to the load: a 199,900 Btu/h unit on an undersized or long gas run will fault under full demand. Budget the PVC or polypropylene vent run with the heater.

Common questions

What is the difference between the NPE-240S2 and the NPE-240A2?

Both are 199,900 Btu/h condensing units. The NPE-240S2 is the standard model at 0.96 UEF. The NPE-240A2 adds ComfortFlow, a built-in recirculation pump and buffer tank, at 0.95 UEF. Compare them in the Navien model comparison.

Can a Navien NPE run on propane?

Yes. The NPE-2 models listed here are NG/LP convertible. NHW700 and NPN models are sold as separate natural gas and propane versions, so check the fuel in the product title.

What venting does a Navien NPE need?

NPE-2 units vent through 2" or 3" PVC, CPVC or polypropylene and need a condensate drain. Use the vent materials and maximum lengths in the installation manual for your model.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Rheem tankless units: RTG non-condensing gas, RTGH condensing gas and the IKONIC condensing line, up to 199,900 Btu/h, with a built-in recirculation pump on some IKONIC models, plus electric models from 8 to 36 kW. Gas models run 120,000 to 199,900 Btu/h and deliver 3.3 to 5.6 GPM at a 70°F rise. Every gas unit takes 3/4" MIP on water and gas, holds 85 to 140°F and modulates down to 11,000 Btu/h.

The choice that decides the installation is condensing or not. The RTG series is non-condensing: 0.81 to 0.82 UEF, a copper heat exchanger, and exhaust hot enough to require 3"/5" concentric venting. The RTGH series condenses: 0.93 UEF, and exhaust cool enough to vent through 2" or 3" PVC, CPVC or polypropylene. Repair parts, vent kits and valve kits are listed separately.

How to choose

  • RTG or RTGH. Compare the heater and the vent material together: the non-condensing RTG indoor models need concentric vent, and the condensing RTGH vents in plastic pipe and needs a condensate drain.
  • IKONIC. The RTGH-S models carry a stainless steel heat exchanger, 0.96 UEF and an elevation rating of 10,200 feet against 8,400 for the other gas series. They run on natural gas or propane. Some IKONIC models add a factory recirculation pump, named in the product title.
  • Indoor or outdoor. The XL suffix is an outdoor model that needs no vent pipe. DV is indoor direct vent.
  • Fuel. RTG and RTGH models are sold as natural gas (N) or propane (P) versions. Check the product title.
  • Gas and electrical supply. Size the gas supply to the load, not to the 3/4" connection. On electric models, check the amperage and breaker requirement before ordering.

Common questions

What is the difference between Rheem RTG and RTGH?

RTG units are non-condensing and need concentric venting. RTGH units are condensing, rated 0.93 UEF, and vent through PVC, CPVC or polypropylene.

What do DV and XL mean in a Rheem model number?

DV is an indoor direct vent model. XL is an outdoor model that needs no vent pipe.

Which Rheem tankless has a built-in recirculation pump?

The IKONIC models titled "with Recirculation Pump" include a factory recirculation pump. For other models, a separate recirculation pump kit is listed under tankless repair parts.

Related: all tankless water heaters, Navien tankless water heaters, Noritz tankless water heaters, Rheem tankless water heater parts and tankless valve kits.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Noritz tankless water heaters across the EZ, NRC, NRCP, NRCR and NR98 series, from 157,000 to 199,900 Btu/h, in natural gas and propane. Minimum inputs are listed at 15,000 to 18,000 Btu/h, so a small draw does not fire the burner at full rate.

Condensing or not is the first decision, and it changes the vent. The EZ, NRCP and NRCR models are listed at 0.95 to 0.96 UEF and the NRC models at 0.89 to 0.91. The NR98 is the non-condensing line, listed at 0.82 UEF, and its SV and DVC versions take different vent systems. Vent kits, conversion kits and parts are listed separately.

How to choose

  • Vent path. Confirm the vent before the unit. Use the vent material, diameter and maximum length in the installation manual for the model. On the NR98, the choice between SV and DVC decides the vent system.
  • Recirculation. The NRCP111 and NRCP98 are listed with a recirculation pump. Choose one of them if you want recirculation without adding a pump.
  • Fuel. LP and NG are separate models here, except the EZ111 Pro, which is field convertible.
  • Gas supply. Size the gas line to the full input and the length of the run, using the tables in the installation manual.

Common questions

Which Noritz tankless water heaters are condensing?

The EZ, NRC, NRCP and NRCR series are condensing. The NR98 is non-condensing and takes a different vent system, so check the installation manual.

Which Noritz models have a recirculation pump?

The NRCP111 and NRCP98 are listed with a recirculation pump. Check the manufacturer's instructions before adding an external recirculation loop to another model.

Can I convert a Noritz tankless water heater between natural gas and propane?

The EZ111 Pro is listed as field convertible. The other models here are sold as separate natural gas and propane versions, so check the fuel in the product title.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Heat pump water heaters move heat from the surrounding air into the tank instead of generating it, so they use less electricity than a standard electric tank. Rheem ProTerra 240 V hybrids, in 50, 65 and 80 gallons, run on a 30 A circuit and keep 4,500 W elements as backup for high demand. The ProTerra 120 V plug-in models (40 and 50 gallon) run on a 120 V circuit, which suits a retrofit where a gas heater is being replaced and there is no 240 V circuit. The Sanco Gen5 is a split system: an outdoor heat pump unit paired with a separate storage tank.

Two things to plan for: the unit needs enough surrounding air volume to work, and it produces condensate that needs a drain or a condensate pump. Set it in a drain pan where a leak would cause damage.

How to choose

  • Voltage. The 240 V ProTerra hybrids need a 240 V, 30 A circuit and add 4,500 W backup elements, which recover faster when demand is high. The 120 V plug-in models suit gas-to-electric replacements with no 240 V circuit at the water heater.
  • Capacity. 240 V hybrids are listed in 50, 65 and 80 gallons; the 120 V plug-in models here are 40 and 50 gallons. Compare the first-hour rating on the spec sheet with your busiest hour.
  • Air space. Check the installation manual for the minimum room size or the ducting option.
  • Condensate. Plan a drain or a condensate pump, as well as the usual relief valve discharge.
  • Leak protection. Some ProTerra models include built-in LeakGuard, named in the product title.

Common questions

Is a hybrid water heater the same as a heat pump water heater?

Yes. Hybrid is the common name for a heat pump water heater that also has electric elements. The heat pump does most of the work, and the elements back it up during high demand.

Do I need a 240V circuit for a heat pump water heater?

Most hybrid models, such as the Rheem ProTerra 50 to 80 gallon units, need a 240 V circuit. The ProTerra 120 V plug-in models run on a 120 V circuit. Where a 240 V circuit is already in place, or the household uses a lot of hot water, the 240 V hybrid is usually the better fit. Check the electrical requirements in the installation manual before ordering.

Does a heat pump water heater need a drain?

Yes. The heat pump makes condensate, so the installation needs a condensate drain or a condensate pump, as well as the usual relief valve discharge. Check the installation manual for the air space the unit needs around it.

Related: electric tank water heaters, Rheem 50 gallon water heaters, condensate pumps, water heater pans and tankless water heaters.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Rheem and Ruud gas tank water heaters for homes: Rheem Professional Classic, Professional Classic Plus and Professional Prestige models, plus Ruud 40 and 50 gallon tanks. Most are 40 and 50 gallon, with sizes from 29 to 98 gallons and inputs from 32,000 to 100,000 Btu/h. Models come in natural gas and propane versions, with atmospheric, powered damper, power vent, direct vent and power direct vent venting.

Size a water heater by its first-hour rating and household peak demand, not tank volume alone. Confirm the gas type, the venting method your space allows, and the height and diameter against the available space. Plan for a T&P relief discharge line, a thermal expansion tank on closed systems, a drain pan where required, and seismic straps in areas that need them.

How to choose

  • Capacity and first-hour rating. Compare the first-hour rating on the spec sheet with your busiest hour of hot water use. A higher Btu/h input recovers faster.
  • Fuel. Natural gas and propane are separate models. The fuel is in the product title.
  • Venting. Atmospheric models vent by natural draft into an existing B-vent or chimney. Powered damper models close the flue between cycles. Power vent models use a blower and plastic pipe through a side wall. Direct vent and power direct vent models also bring combustion air in from outside.
  • Height. Short models fit under a low ceiling; check the height and diameter, including clearance above for the connections.
  • Relief valve location. Some models have a factory-installed top T&P valve, noted in the title.

Common questions

What size gas water heater do I need, 40 or 50 gallon?

Go by the first-hour rating, not the tank size alone. Compare the first-hour rating on the spec sheet with the hot water your household uses in its busiest hour. Two tanks of the same volume can differ because a higher input recovers faster.

What is the difference between atmospheric, power vent and direct vent?

An atmospheric water heater vents by natural draft into a B-vent or chimney. A power vent model uses a blower to push exhaust through plastic pipe out a side wall. A direct vent model takes its combustion air from outside. Match the vent type to the house before comparing anything else.

Which Ruud gas water heaters are listed here?

The Ruud gas models listed here are 40 and 50 gallon natural gas and propane tanks.

Related: Rheem 40 gallon water heaters, Rheem 50 gallon water heaters, electric tank water heaters, water heater gas supplies and water heater pans.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Rheem Professional Classic, Classic Plus and Prestige electric tank water heaters from about 20 to 50 gallons, plus Ruud 40 and 50 gallon models. They run at 240 volts with 4.5 kW or 5.5 kW elements, in short, medium and tall heights. Classic Plus models include LeakSense leak detection, Prestige models include LeakGuard, and Demand Response models are marked in the product title.

Size by first-hour rating and household demand, and check the height and diameter against the space. Confirm the circuit voltage, breaker and wire size for the element wattage. Plan for a T&P relief discharge line, a thermal expansion tank on closed systems, a drain pan where required, and seismic straps in areas that need them.

How to choose

  • Capacity. Compare the first-hour rating on the spec sheet with your busiest hour of hot water use.
  • Height. The same capacity comes in short, medium and tall tanks. Measure the space, including clearance above for the connections.
  • Element wattage and circuit. 4.5 kW and 5.5 kW models at 240 V need the breaker and wire size given in the installation manual.
  • Leak detection. LeakSense and LeakGuard models are named in the product title.
  • Demand response. Check whether your utility or local code calls for a demand response ready water heater.

Common questions

What circuit does a 240 V electric water heater need?

It depends on the element wattage. Use the breaker and wire size listed in the installation manual and on the rating plate for the model, and follow local electrical code.

What is the difference between short, medium and tall electric water heaters?

The capacity can be the same; the shape differs. Short and medium tanks fit under a low ceiling or a stair, and a tall tank is narrower for a tight closet.

Is a heat pump water heater an alternative to a standard electric tank?

Yes. A heat pump water heater uses less electricity but needs air space around it and a condensate drain. See heat pump water heaters.

Related: Rheem 50 gallon water heaters, Rheem 40 gallon water heaters, gas tank water heaters, elements and electric conversion kits and water heater pans.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Rheem 40 gallon water heaters, gas and electric, on one page: Professional Classic®, Professional Classic Plus® and Professional Prestige® residential tanks, light-duty commercial electric, and models listed for manufactured housing.

Gas or electric follows the house. Replace like for like unless you are prepared to run a new gas line or a 240 V circuit. Gas input on these runs from 30,000 to 50,000 Btu/h, and a higher input recovers faster after a long shower. The residential electrics are 240 V at 4.5 or 5.5 kW; the light-duty commercial electrics are 208 V at 6 kW. Manufactured homes need a manufactured-housing model. The MH units here are listed for that use, including direct-vent versions that take combustion air from outside the closet.

How to choose

  • Fuel. Natural gas, propane or electric. The fuel and the input are in the product title.
  • Venting on gas. Atmospheric models vent by natural draft into an existing B-vent or chimney. Powered damper (PD) models close the flue between cycles to cut standby loss. Power vent (PV) models use a blower to push exhaust through plastic pipe out a side wall, and power direct vent (PDV) models also bring combustion air in from outside. Match the vent to the house before comparing anything else.
  • Height on electric. The same 40 gallons comes in a medium height for a low ceiling or under a stair, and a tall, narrower tank for a tight closet. Measure the space, including clearance above for the connections.
  • Voltage. Residential electric models are 240 V; the light-duty commercial electric models are 208 V.
  • Input. A higher Btu/h input recovers faster.

Common questions

Is a 40 gallon water heater big enough?

Compare the first-hour rating on the spec sheet with the hot water your household uses in its busiest hour. If you need more, see Rheem 50 gallon water heaters.

Which Rheem 40 gallon gas water heater replaces an atmospheric model?

Replace like for like: an atmospheric model vents into the existing B-vent or chimney. Power vent and power direct vent models need plastic vent pipe through a side wall and an electrical supply for the blower.

What do PD, PV, PDV and DV mean in a Rheem model number?

PD is powered damper, PV is power vent, PDV is power direct vent and DV is direct vent. The letters appear at the end of the model number in the product title.

Related: Rheem 50 gallon water heaters, gas tank water heaters, electric tank water heaters, water heater connectors and water heater pans.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Rheem 50 gallon water heaters in one place: Professional Classic®, Classic Plus® and Prestige® residential gas and electric tanks, high-input Prestige® Maximus gas models, ProTerra® hybrid and 120 V plug-in heat pump water heaters, and commercial units.

Gas models are listed in natural gas and propane, with inputs from 33,000 to 100,000 Btu/h, in atmospheric, powered damper, power vent, direct vent and power direct vent versions. Residential electric models run on 240 V with 4.5 or 5.5 kW elements, in medium and tall heights. The commercial models include the Triton® light duty gas unit and heavy duty 208 V three-phase electric units. Compare the first-hour rating on the spec sheet with your busiest hour of use.

How to choose

  • Start with the fuel the house already has. Like for like avoids a new gas line or a 240 V circuit.
  • On gas, match the venting. Atmospheric models use an existing B-vent or chimney. Powered damper models close the flue when idle. Power vent and power direct vent models use a blower and plastic pipe through a side wall.
  • Input. A higher Btu/h input recovers faster.
  • On electric, check height and circuit. Residential models run on 240 V with 4.5 or 5.5 kW elements, in medium and tall heights.
  • Heat pump. A ProTerra model uses less electricity than a standard electric tank but needs air space and a condensate drain.

Common questions

Which Rheem 50 gallon gas water heater should I choose?

Match the venting first: atmospheric for an existing B-vent or chimney, power vent or power direct vent for a side wall, direct vent where combustion air must come from outside. Then compare input and first-hour rating.

Is 50 gallons enough for my household?

Compare the first-hour rating on the spec sheet with your busiest hour of hot water use. If 50 gallons is more than you need, see Rheem 40 gallon water heaters.

Can I replace a 50 gallon gas water heater with a heat pump model?

Yes, if the space has the air volume the unit needs, a condensate drain and a suitable circuit. The 50 gallon ProTerra 120 V plug-in model runs on a 120 V circuit; the 240 V hybrid needs a 240 V, 30 A circuit. Check the electrical requirements in the installation manual.

Commercial gas water heaters from 76,000 through 400,000 Btu/h and 50 to 100 gallons, in natural gas and propane. The range includes Rheem Triton® light duty and heavy duty models, Rheem Universal and medium duty commercial tanks, models with ASME construction, and the Noritz Hybrid Hot commercial tankless with storage.

Commercial sizing works from first-hour rating and not from tank volume. That figure, storage plus recovery combined, is what determines whether a restaurant or a locker room runs out at peak. A large tank with slow recovery and a small tank with fast recovery can carry the same rating. Units at 90% efficiency and above are condensing: the condensing models here are listed for PVC, CPVC or polypropylene venting and need a condensate drain with neutralization, since the condensate is acidic. Most water connections are 1-1/2" or 2".

How to choose

  • First-hour rating. Size from peak-hour demand, using storage and recovery together.
  • Input. Inputs here run from 76,000 to 400,000 Btu/h. Confirm the gas supply and meter can carry the input.
  • Venting. A condensing replacement in a building plumbed for atmospheric venting means new vent, a new drain and often a new gas line. The atmospheric models here are listed for B-vent.
  • ASME construction. Models marked ASME are built to the ASME code, which some jurisdictions and applications require. Check with the local authority.
  • Fuel. Natural gas and propane are separate models, named in the title.

Common questions

How do I size a commercial gas water heater?

Work from the first-hour rating, which combines storage and recovery, and compare it with the peak-hour demand of the fixtures and equipment served.

When is an ASME water heater required?

Requirements depend on the input, the storage volume and the jurisdiction. Ask the local authority or the project engineer, and choose a model marked ASME Construction where it is required.

Can a condensing commercial water heater use the existing vent?

No. A condensing unit needs the plastic vent system named in its installation manual and a condensate drain with neutralization. Follow the venting section of the installation manual.

Related: commercial electric water heaters, furnace and water heater venting, condensate neutralizers, mixing valves and all water heating.

Commercial electric water heaters from Rheem, from 30 to 120 gallons. Light duty models come with 6 kW elements at 208 V and a fused terminal block, or with triple-rated elements (3.4 kW at 208 V, 4.5 kW at 240 V, 6 kW at 277 V). Heavy duty models are 208 V three-phase at 15, 18 or 36 kW. Maximum delivery temperatures in this collection are 170°F, 180°F and 181°F.

Recovery is a function of total kW and is the number to size from, alongside storage volume. The temperature rating is the specification to check against the application: a commercial dishwasher that needs a 180°F sanitizing rinse cannot be served by a heater that tops out below that without a booster. Connections are 3/4" and 1-1/2" NPT dielectric nipples.

How to choose

  • Voltage and phase. Order the heater for the voltage and phase available at the panel, such as 208 V, 240 V or 277 V. Some models are field-convertible between voltages, which is listed on the product page.
  • Total kW. Recovery follows kW. Compare storage and recovery with the peak-hour demand.
  • Delivery temperature. Check the maximum temperature against the equipment served. Use a thermostatic mixing valve downstream where the code limits the temperature at fixtures.
  • Height. ELDS models are the short versions of the ELD light duty tanks.
  • Terminal block. Choose a fused terminal block model where the electrical code or the installation manual requires it.

Common questions

How do I size a commercial electric water heater?

Size from peak-hour hot water demand: storage volume covers the first draw, and recovery, set by total kW, covers the rest of the hour. Compare both numbers on the product page with the demand of the fixtures and equipment served.

Does the heater voltage have to match the building?

Yes. Order the heater for the voltage and phase available at the panel, such as 208 V, 240 V or 277 V. Some models are field-convertible between voltages, which is listed on the product page.

What is a fused terminal block?

A fused terminal block adds fuses in the heater's wiring compartment, protecting the element circuits inside the heater. It is required on some larger commercial heaters; check the local electrical code and the installation manual.

Related: commercial gas water heaters, elements and electric conversion kits, mixing valves, residential electric water heaters and all water heating.

This collection gathers Rheem-brand replacement parts listed under Rheem part numbers, many of them in the SP series, so you can match the number on the old part or in the unit's parts list.

For gas tank heaters you will find gas control thermostats, combination gas control kits, burner assemblies, pilot and igniter assemblies, hot surface igniters, ignition controls and vent hoods. Electric models are covered with screw-in heating elements in several voltages and wattages, thermostats and conversion kit assemblies for ELD and ELDS commercial heaters. Dip tubes and anode rods are listed for tank maintenance. Tankless parts include flame rods, controller kits, cable kits, inlet water filters, recirculation pump kits and concentric vent components for RTG and RTGH models.

How to choose

  • Part number. Match the Rheem part number on the old part or in the parts list for the heater.
  • Model and serial number. Confirm both on the rating plate before ordering, because elements, controls and vent parts are model-specific.
  • Fuel. Gas controls and pilot assemblies are specific to natural gas or propane.
  • Voltage and wattage. Elements and conversion kits are listed by voltage (208, 240 or 480 V) and kW. Match the rating plate and the supply.
  • Who does the work. Leave gas control and burner work to a qualified technician.

Common questions

How do I find the right Rheem water heater part?

Use the model and serial number on the rating plate to find the parts list for your heater, then match the Rheem part number. Many are in the SP series.

Can I change the voltage or wattage of a Rheem commercial electric water heater?

Conversion kit assemblies are listed for ELD and ELDS models by voltage and kW. Check the installation manual for the conversions allowed on your model.

Are Rheem tankless parts in this collection?

Yes. Flame rods, igniters, control kits, recirculation pump kits and vent components for RTG and RTGH models are listed here and under Rheem tankless water heater parts.

Drain pans for water heaters and appliances, from 19 to 36 inches. The collection includes IPS aluminum and plastic pans from 20 to 30 inches inside diameter, IPS ToughPan Pro and ToughPan Dry Lift pans, Smitty Pan round metal pans from 19 to 36 inches, and Camco aluminum pans from 20 to 30 inches. Pans come with a PVC or CPVC drain connection, a side drain hole, or no hole. Washing machine pans from Smitty Pan, Oatey and Camco are listed here as well.

Choose a pan with an inside diameter a few inches larger than the water heater, and check the side height and material required by local code. Pipe the drain fitting to an approved location. Place the pan on a level surface before setting the heater.

How to choose

  • Diameter. Measure the water heater and pick an inside diameter a few inches larger. IPS lists both inside and outside diameter in the title.
  • Material. Aluminum, plastic or metal. Check the material and side height your local code requires, especially under gas water heaters.
  • Drain connection. PVC or CPVC, 1" or 1" x 1-1/2", or no connection.
  • Hole position. Side-hole pans drain through the wall of the pan; no-hole pans are for locations with no drain line or for a field-cut opening.

Common questions

What size drain pan do I need for a water heater?

Choose a pan with an inside diameter a few inches larger than the diameter of the water heater. Check the heater's diameter on its spec sheet.

Is a drain pan required under a water heater?

Many plumbing codes require a pan where a leak would cause damage, such as in an attic or on a finished floor. Check your local code for where a pan is required and what material it must be.

PVC or CPVC drain fitting?

Pans here are listed with either a PVC or a CPVC drain connection. Use the material your local code calls for.

Thermal expansion tanks for potable water systems, from compact tanks for tankless heaters to 10.2 gallons, with mounting brackets. Models include the Amtrol Therm-X-Trol ST-5 (2 gallon) and ST-12 (4.4 gallon), the Flexcon PH-5 (2 gallon), PH-12 (4.8 gallon) and PH-25 (10.2 gallon), and the Zilmet ZEP1 for tankless water heaters. Connections are 1/2" and 3/4" MIP.

These exist because of the check valve or backflow preventer on the incoming service. Once that device is fitted, the plumbing becomes a closed system: water heated in the tank expands and has nowhere to go, so pressure climbs until the T&P relief valve weeps. A potable tank is not a hydronic tank. It must be rated for drinking water.

How to choose

  • Tank volume. Size from the water heater capacity, the supply pressure and the temperature setting, using the manufacturer's sizing chart.
  • Potable rating. Use a tank rated for drinking water on a water heater. Hydronic tanks belong on a boiler loop.
  • Connection. Match the connection, 1/2" or 3/4" MIP on the tanks here, to the cold supply tee.
  • Pre-charge. Pre-charge the tank to match your static water pressure before installing it, with no water in it. Charging afterwards reads the water side, not the air.
  • Support. Use a wall mount bracket where the tank is not supported by the piping.

Common questions

Why is my water heater relief valve dripping?

On a closed system, water heated in the tank expands and pressure climbs until the T&P relief valve weeps. A weeping relief valve on a recently re-plumbed house is often this and not a faulty valve. A thermal expansion tank on the cold inlet absorbs the expansion.

Where does a water heater expansion tank go?

On the cold water supply to the water heater, between the heater and the check valve, backflow preventer or pressure reducing valve. Follow the tank manufacturer's installation instructions.

Can I use a boiler expansion tank on a water heater?

No. A water heater needs a potable tank rated for drinking water. Tanks for hydronic heating are listed under expansion tanks for heating.

Related: all expansion tanks, water heater T&P relief valves, pressure reducing valves, water heater connectors and water heater pans.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Venting components for condensing gas appliances: polypropylene single wall pipe and fittings, water heater vent kits, terminations and vent screens, and concentric vents, from Centrotherm, Noritz, Rheem, US Boiler, IPEX and DiversiTech. Vent pipe and fittings run 2" through 10".

A condensing appliance does not vent like an atmospheric one. A non-condensing furnace or an atmospheric water heater sends hot, dry flue gas up a chimney or a B-vent on its own buoyancy. A condensing furnace, boiler or tankless heater pulls most of that heat out first, so what leaves the appliance is cool, wet and acidic, and a fan pushes it. That is why these systems are sealed, sloped and fan-rated. Some products here name UL 1738 in the title, the standard for venting systems for gas appliances with condensing flue gases.

How to choose

  • Vent material. The appliance installation manual decides the vent material. Where PVC or CPVC is used as vent, it is because the appliance manufacturer's instructions permit it. Do not mix parts from different vent systems unless the manufacturers allow it.
  • Single wall or concentric. Single wall runs exhaust and intake as two separate pipes and needs two penetrations with a minimum separation at the terminations. A concentric vent carries intake around exhaust in one pipe, so the building gets one penetration and one termination.
  • Diameter and length. Use the diameter, maximum length and number of elbows in the appliance manual.
  • Terminations. Clearance to windows, doors, soffits, air intakes, gas meters and grade is set by code and by the appliance manual. Vent screens here cover 2" through 8".
  • Retrofit and condensate. Flexible polypropylene liner in 25' and 35' kits relines an existing chase. Slope vent runs back toward the appliance so condensate drains to its trap.

Common questions

Can I vent a tankless water heater with PVC?

Only if the installation manual for that model permits it. Condensing units are commonly approved for PVC, CPVC or polypropylene; non-condensing units use the vent system their manual names. The manual also sets the diameter and maximum length.

What is UL 1738 vent pipe?

UL 1738 is the standard for venting systems for gas appliances with condensing flue gases. Check the product title or the manufacturer's documentation for the listing.

Can a condensing appliance vent into an existing chimney?

Not directly. An existing masonry chimney or B-vent is not built for cool, wet flue gas. A flexible polypropylene liner kit can be run down the existing chase where the appliance manual allows it.

Related: polypropylene vent pipe, water heater vent kits, vent terminations, gas tankless water heaters and condensate pumps.

Hot water boilers for residential and light commercial hydronic heating, from 38,000 to 399,000 BTU/h input. The collection holds three types. Condensing boilers, such as the Navien NHB-H and NFB-H, IBC SL and VX, US Boiler Alta and Aspen and Lochinvar KHB, WHB and Noble, vent through plastic or stainless pipe; the IBC and US Boiler models are listed at 95 to 96 percent efficiency. Cast iron boilers, the US Boiler (Burnham) Series 2e chimney vented and X-PV power vented models, are listed at 84 to 85 percent and suit older high-temperature radiator systems. Combi boilers, such as the Navien NCB-H and NFC-H and the IBC CX and SFC, add domestic hot water on demand to space heating.

A condensing boiler reaches its rated efficiency only when the return water is cool enough to condense the flue gas, so the emitters and controls matter as much as the boiler.

How to choose

  • BTU input: size the boiler from a heat-loss calculation for the building, not from the rating plate of the old boiler.
  • Boiler type and return temperature: a condensing boiler needs low return water temperature, which means radiant floor, panel radiators sized for lower water temperature or an outdoor reset control. A cast iron boiler tolerates high return temperature and needs a bypass or mixing arrangement to protect it against thermal shock.
  • Fuel: Navien boilers are listed as natural gas and propane convertible. For other brands, check the gas type in the product title.
  • Venting: Series 2e boilers are chimney vented and X-PV boilers are power vented. Condensing boilers need PVC, polypropylene or stainless venting plus a neutralized condensate drain.
  • Circulator and elevation: product titles state "Includes Grundfos Pump" or "No Pump Included" and give the elevation range, such as 0-2,000 ft or 0-10,000 ft.

Common questions

Condensing or cast iron boiler?

A condensing boiler reaches its rated efficiency only with low return water temperature, such as radiant floor or an outdoor reset control. A cast iron boiler tolerates high return temperature and suits older high-temperature radiator systems.

Does the boiler include a circulator pump?

Check the product title. Many listings say Includes Grundfos Pump or No Pump Included. If no pump is included, add one from circulator pumps.

What size boiler do I need?

Size the boiler from a heat-loss calculation for the building, not from the rating of the old boiler. Older boilers were often oversized. For a combi, also check the hot water side: a combi that heats the house can still be short for two showers at once.

Shop by type or brand: condensing boilers, combi boilers, cast iron gas boilers, Navien boilers and Burnham boilers.

collection.descriptionHtml:
A condensing boiler recovers extra heat by cooling the flue gas until its water vapor condenses. The collection includes Navien NHB-H wall-hung boilers from 55,000 to 150,000 BTU/h and NFB models from 175,000 to 399,000 BTU/h, IBC SL G3 fire tube boilers from 85,000 to 260,000 BTU/h and the IBC VX series, US Boiler (Burnham) Alta water tube and Aspen fire tube boilers, and Lochinvar KHB, WHB and Noble boilers. The IBC and US Boiler models are listed at 95 to 96 percent efficiency, with listed elevation ranges of up to 10,000 to 12,000 feet depending on the model.

These boilers reach their rated efficiency only with low return water temperatures, so review the emitters and the controls before choosing one.

How to choose

  • BTU input and turndown: size the boiler to a room-by-room heat-loss calculation, and check the turndown ratio so it modulates well at low loads. Navien NHB-H titles list up to 15:1 turndown.
  • Return water temperature: radiant floors, low-temperature emitters and outdoor reset controls keep the return water cool enough for the boiler to condense.
  • Venting: confirm the vent material and the maximum vent length for the model. Sealed-combustion condensing boilers vent in PVC, CPVC, polypropylene or stainless, as the manufacturer lists.
  • Fuel and elevation: Navien models are listed as natural gas and propane convertible. Check the gas type, the gas supply size and the elevation range in the title.
  • Pump and condensate: Alta titles list an included Grundfos pump, while Aspen, SL and VX titles list no pump. Plan a condensate drain and a neutralizer.

Common questions

Why does a condensing boiler need low return water temperature?

It only condenses flue gas, and reaches its rated efficiency, when return water is cool enough. Radiant floors, low-temperature emitters and outdoor reset controls help.

Does a condensing boiler need a condensate neutralizer?

The condensate is acidic, so most installations need a drain and a neutralizer. See condensate neutralizers.

What venting does a condensing boiler use?

Sealed-combustion condensing boilers vent in PVC, CPVC, polypropylene or stainless, as the manufacturer lists. Check the maximum vent length for your model.

A combi boiler provides space heating and domestic hot water on demand from one unit, so there is no separate water heater or indirect tank. The collection includes IBC CX combi boilers at 150,000 and 199,000 BTU/h with 10:1 turndown, IBC SFC combi boilers from 125,000 to 199,000 BTU/h listed at 94 to 95 percent efficiency, and Navien NCB-H and NFC-H condensing combi boilers with 60,000 to 199,900 BTU/h of heating input and up to 210,000 BTU/h for hot water.

Domestic hot water demand usually sets the input of a combi, so a model that heats the house well can still be short for two showers running at once. Check both sides before ordering.

How to choose

  • Heating input: it must cover the calculated heat loss of the building. Check the minimum firing rate if the system has small zones.
  • Hot water input: the domestic side has to keep up with the fixtures that run at the same time. Navien titles list both figures, for example 110,000 BTU/h heating and 199,900 BTU/h hot water on the NCB-240/110H.
  • Fuel and gas line: Navien NFC-H models and the NCB-240/110H are listed as natural gas and propane convertible. Size the gas line for the full input.
  • Venting and condensate: confirm the venting options for the model and plan a condensate drain.
  • System pump: the IBC SFC160-1 title lists a built-in pump; the SFC125 and SFC199 titles list no pump included.

Common questions

How do I size a combi boiler?

Check two numbers: the heating input must cover the heat loss, and the hot water side must keep up with the fixtures that run at the same time. Hot water demand usually sets the input.

Combi boiler or boiler with an indirect tank?

A combi saves space because there is no tank. A boiler with an indirect water heater stores hot water and handles several fixtures at once more easily.

Is a system pump included?

It depends on the model. Check the product title and specifications before ordering.

Related collections: Navien combi boilers, condensing boilers, indirect water heaters, IBC boilers and parts and condensate neutralizers.

A Navien combi boiler heats the home and makes domestic hot water on demand from one wall-hung condensing unit, so there is no separate water heater or indirect tank. Two series are listed here. The NCB-H pairs 60,000 to 150,000 BTU/h of heating input with 160,000 or 199,900 BTU/h for hot water: the NCB-190/060H, NCB-190/080H, NCB-240/110H, NCB-240/130H and NCB-250/150H. The larger NFC-H, the NFC-250/175H and NFC-250/200H, offers 175,000 or 199,900 BTU/h of heating with 210,000 BTU/h for hot water.

All are indoor wall-hung models.

How to choose

  • Heating input: it should cover the calculated heat loss of the building. The NCB-H runs from 60,000 to 150,000 BTU/h and the NFC-H is 175,000 or 199,900 BTU/h.
  • Hot water input: the hot water side has to keep up with the fixtures that run at the same time, so check the hot water flow at your temperature rise. Inputs are 160,000 BTU/h on the NCB-190, 199,900 BTU/h on the NCB-240 and NCB-250, and 210,000 BTU/h on the NFC-250.
  • Fuel: the NCB-240/110H and both NFC-H models are listed as natural gas and propane convertible. Size the gas line for the full input.
  • Venting and condensate: plan the vent run from the installation manual and a condensate drain with a neutralizer.
  • Side-by-side specs: compare every model in the Navien model comparison.

Common questions

What is the difference between the NCB-240/110H and the NCB-240/130H?

Both have 199,900 BTU/h of input for hot water. The NCB-240/110H has 110,000 BTU/h of heating input and the NCB-240/130H has 130,000 BTU/h.

NCB-H or NFC-H?

The NCB-H covers heating inputs up to 150,000 BTU/h. The NFC-H is the larger series, with 175,000 or 199,900 BTU/h of heating input and 210,000 BTU/h for hot water.

Can a Navien combi replace my boiler and water heater?

Yes. A combi heats the home and makes domestic hot water on demand from one wall-hung unit. Size it for both the heat loss and the fixtures that run at the same time.

collection.descriptionHtml:
When a boiler stops heating, short-cycles or leaks, the fix is usually one part, not a new boiler. This collection brings together replacement parts for boilers, listed by manufacturer part number so you can match the number on the old part or in the boiler parts list.

Controls and ignition: aquastats and immersion wells (Resideo L8148, L4006, L4008), gas valves, hot surface igniters, ignition modules, pilot burners, thermocouples and low water cut-offs. Water side: pressure relief valves, fill and feed valves, expansion tanks, air eliminators, air vents, boiler drains, gauges and boiler trim kits. The collection also holds Taco and Grundfos circulators and US Boiler (Burnham) factory parts.

How to choose

  • Part number: match the number on the old part or in the boiler parts list. Check the boiler model and serial number on the rating plate first.
  • Voltage: controls are listed as 24 V, 120 V or millivolt. Match the control circuit of the boiler.
  • Connection size: compare the thread or sweat size of the old part, such as 1/2" or 3/4" NPT on immersion wells and 3/4" on boiler relief valves.
  • Relief valve rating: match the set pressure marked on the old valve and on the boiler rating plate.
  • Brand parts: US Boiler kits are matched to a series, an input size or a section count, so read the full title.

Common questions

How do I find the right boiler part?

Start with the boiler model and serial number on the rating plate, then match the part number on the old part, its voltage and its connection size. Our zone valve replacement guide and the Zone Planner can help with zoning parts.

Can I replace a gas valve or ignition control myself?

Gas valve, ignition and burner work should be done by a qualified heating technician.

Which parts control boiler pressure?

The fill valve keeps the system at its cold-fill pressure, the expansion tank takes up the water volume as it heats, and the relief valve opens if pressure reaches its set point.

Go straight to aquastats and wells, boiler fill valves, circulator pumps, zone valves or US Boiler / Burnham parts.

How to choose

  • Model and serial number: read both from the data plate of the appliance before ordering.
  • Vent diameter: wall flange and vent terminator kits are listed in 2" and 3", and concentric elbows in 80-125 mm. Match the vent system already installed.
  • Termination type: sidewall termination kits are listed in 11.5" and 21", and the concentric roof termination in 13" with adjustable roof flashing. Terminations have code and manufacturer clearances from windows, doors, soffits and property lines.

  • Racks and manifolds: the Ready-Link Rack (V4) base and add-on are listed for NPE, NCB, NFB and NHB units; primary manifolds are separate for NHB and NFB.

Common questions

How do I find the right Navien part?

Order from the data plate, using the full model and serial number. Most parts are model-specific.

Will an NPE vent kit fit an NCB combi boiler?

No. Vent kits are model-specific, and a vent kit for an NPE is not an NCB kit. Check the kit title against your model.

Which Navien series have a parts kit here?

Series parts kits are listed for NPE, NPE-2, NCB and NCB-E, NFB-H, NFC-H and NR/NP units. Pick the kit named for your series.

For complete units, see all Navien products, Navien combi boilers, Navien boilers and Navien tankless water heaters. Parts for other tankless brands are in tankless repair parts.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Replacement parts and kits for US Boiler (Burnham) boilers, listed by factory part number. U.S. Boiler Company makes the Burnham residential boilers, so Burnham part numbers are supported here. The collection includes gas valves, Ebm-Papst blowers, ignitors and flame sensors, fuse sets, temperature sensors and service kits for Alta, Phantom II and K2WT boilers; Alpine ignitor and flame sensor gasket sets; natural gas to propane conversion kits by section count; direct vent conversion kits for X-PV; IQ low water cut-off and outdoor reset kits; and flexible double-wall oil vent and a Beckett AFG air intake and vent kit for oil boilers.

Kits are matched to a specific series, input size or section count, so confirm the boiler model, section count and serial number on the rating plate before ordering.

How to choose

  • Series and model: titles name the boilers each part fits, such as Alta, Alpine, Aspen, K2WT, Phantom II, X-PV and MPO-IQ.
  • Input size: many parts are split by input in MBH, for example blowers for 080-136 MBH and for 150-200 MBH.
  • Section count: gas conversion kits are listed for 2, 3-6 and 7-9 section boilers, and direct vent conversion kits for 3 to 8 sections.
  • Altitude: the natural gas to propane conversion kits are listed for 0-2,000 ft. Check the altitude limit before ordering.
  • Gas valve size: electronic ignition gas valves are listed in 1/2" x 1/2" and 3/4" x 3/4".

Common questions

How do I find the right US Boiler part?

Use the boiler model, section count and serial number from the rating plate. Kits are matched to specific series such as Alta, Alpine, MPO-IQ, Series 2e and X-PV.

Are Burnham and US Boiler parts the same?

Yes. U.S. Boiler Company makes the Burnham residential boilers, so Burnham part numbers are supported under US Boiler.

Can I replace a gas valve or safety control myself?

Gas valves, limits and venting changes should be replaced by a qualified technician and checked with a combustion test after installation.

Related collections: all US Boiler products, Burnham boilers, cast iron gas boilers, boiler parts and low water cut-offs.

collection.descriptionHtml:
An indirect water heater makes domestic hot water using heat from a boiler. Hot boiler water circulates through a coil inside the tank and heats the potable water around it, so the tank has no burner or flue of its own. The collection includes IBC indirect tanks in 444 stainless steel with an aquastat, from 26.8 to 119 gallons, including the DTI-40, DTI-55, DTI-65, DTI-80 and DTI-80MAX; AquaFlow stainless steel indirect-fired water heaters from 30 to 119 gallons (AF-30 through AF-119); Heat-Flo 30 and 40 gallon indirect tanks with top connections and a 60 gallon high-output model with an element; and Lochinvar stainless steel single-wall hot water makers.

Because the tank stores hot water, it handles several fixtures running at once more easily than an on-demand combi.

How to choose

  • Tank capacity: size the tank to the peak hot water demand of the household. Sizes here run from 26.8 to 119 gallons.
  • Boiler output: check the boiler output available for the hot water zone and the first hour rating of the tank at your boiler supply temperature.
  • Coil connections: confirm the connection size and position. The IBC DTI-80MAX and the 119 gallon IBC tank list 1-1/2" inlets, and Heat-Flo tanks list top connections.
  • Control and piping: IBC tanks come with an aquastat. Decide whether the tank will be piped as a priority zone.
  • Safety valves: install a T&P relief valve, and a thermostatic mixing valve where required.

Common questions

How does an indirect water heater work?

Hot water from the boiler runs through a coil inside the tank and heats the potable water around it. The tank has no burner or flue of its own.

What size indirect water heater do I need?

Size it to peak hot water demand and to the boiler output available for the hot water zone. Check the first hour rating and the coil connections.

Which indirect tanks are stainless steel?

The IBC tanks are listed as 444 stainless steel and the AquaFlow tanks as stainless steel. Check the product details for other brands.

Related collections: boilers, condensing boilers, Heat-Flo, mixing valves and water heater T&P relief valves.

collection.descriptionHtml:
A circulator moves water around a closed loop instead of lifting it from a source, so it is sized for flow and head loss through the piping, not for pressure. The collection includes Taco 00 series circulators such as the 007, 0010 and 0015, Taco ECM models such as the 007e, 0015e3 and 0018e, Grundfos UPS15-58FC, UPS26-99, ALPHA and MAGNA circulators, Grundfos UP15 bronze pumps and Resideo ECM and 3-speed circulators.

Fixed-speed circulators run on one curve and are matched to the loop at installation. Variable-speed ECM circulators adjust their own speed, which matters most on systems with zone valves, where the flow demand changes as zones open and close. An oversized pump shows up as noise and short-cycling, and an undersized one leaves cold zones at the end of the run.

How to choose

  • Flow and head: work out the flow in GPM and the head loss in feet for the loop, then compare them with the pump curve. Some titles list the maximum figures, such as 19 ft of head and 18 gpm on the Grundfos UPS15-58FC.
  • Body material: cast iron bodies are for closed hydronic loops only, because the oxygen in fresh water corrodes them. Open loops and potable water, such as domestic hot water recirculation, need a stainless steel or bronze body.
  • Connection: pumps are listed as flanged, union or sweat. Match the flange spacing and size of the pump being replaced.
  • Voltage: most models here are listed at 115 V; Grundfos MAGNA models are listed at 115-230 V.
  • Speed and options: choose fixed speed, 3-speed, ECM variable speed or Delta-T control, with or without an integral flow check (IFC).

Common questions

How do I size a circulator pump?

Size the pump from the flow and head loss of the loop, not from pressure. An oversized pump is noisy and an undersized one leaves cold zones.

Cast iron, bronze or stainless steel?

Use cast iron on closed hydronic heating loops. Use bronze or stainless steel for potable water and hot water recirculation.

What do I need to match when replacing a circulator?

Most residential circulators use the standard flange bolt pattern, so replacing one is usually a matter of matching the flange spacing and the electrical supply. Check the flow and head of the old pump as well.

Shop by type or brand: Taco circulator pumps, Grundfos, variable speed circulators, hot water recirculating pumps and pump flanges and accessories.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Zone valves, replacement heads and parts for hydronic heating, plus dampers and panels for forced-air zoning. The collection includes Honeywell V8043 and V4043 2-way and V8044 and V4044 3-way zone valves, VC series valves, actuators and cartridges, VU fan coil valves, Taco Zone Sentry, QuickTop and heat motor valves, Caleffi and Viega products, Honeywell TrueZONE panels and zone dampers. Connections are sweat, press, flare and NPT in 1/2" through 1". The V8043 and VC lines are now made by Resideo under the same numbers.

Most residential zone valves fail at the powerhead, not the valve body. Replacement heads swap without draining the system, which is the simpler fix when a zone stops responding but the valve still moves by hand.

Popular part numbers: Honeywell V8043A1011, Honeywell V8043E1137, Honeywell 40003916-021, Honeywell VCZZ1100, Honeywell VU842A1046.

How to choose

  • Voltage: V8043 and V8044 valves are listed at 24 Vac, and V4043 and V4044 valves at 120 Vac. Match the old valve and the zone control.
  • Size and connection: match the pipe size (1/2", 3/4" or 1") and the sweat, flare, NPT or press connection. Fan coil valves also list a Cv in the title.
  • Valve action: choose 2-way or 3-way (diverting), and normally closed or normally open, to match the valve being replaced.
  • End switch: pick a valve or head with an end switch if the old one had one.
  • Circulator: as zones close, flow through the remaining ones rises, so a valve-zoned system usually wants a pressure bypass or a variable-speed circulator.

Common questions

Can I replace just the zone valve head?

Often, yes. If the valve body still opens and closes by hand, a replacement head fixes the zone without draining the system.

Normally open or normally closed?

A normally closed valve stays shut until the thermostat powers it open. A normally open valve stays open until it is powered closed. Match the old valve.

What does the end switch do?

The end switch closes when the valve is fully open and tells the boiler or circulator to run. Pick a valve with an end switch if the old one had one.

Shop by brand or part: Honeywell zone valves, Taco zone valves, replacement heads, switching relays and zone controls and variable speed circulators.

collection.descriptionHtml:
An aquastat switches a burner or a circulator according to water temperature. This collection covers Resideo aquastat controls and immersion wells for boilers and water heaters: L8148 aquastat relays, L4006 immersion aquastats, including 100 to 240 °F models, L4008 high limit controls with capillary, L6006 and L6008 high or low limit and circulator controllers, the L7224U universal electronic oil aquastat, copper immersion wells in 1/2" and 3/4" NPT with 3" insertion depth, and heat conductive grease. Resideo makes the Honeywell Home aquastat line under the same model numbers.

Popular part numbers: Resideo L8148E1299, Resideo L4006E1125, Resideo L4008E1156, Resideo L6006C1018, Resideo L7224U1002, Resideo 120650.

How to choose

  • Function: decide whether the control must break on rise as a high limit, make on fall as a low limit, or run a circulator. Check the switching action, SPST or SPDT.
  • Temperature range and differential: confirm the setpoint range covers the application, for example 100-240 °F with a 5-30 °F adjustable differential on the L4006A.
  • Reset: some high limits are listed with manual reset. Match the old control.
  • Well: many controls are sold "less well". Match the well size and insertion depth to the tapping and the control bulb, and apply heat conductive grease for accurate sensing.
  • Voltage: check the control circuit; the L8148E1299 relay is listed for low voltage and millivolt systems.

Common questions

How do I choose a replacement aquastat?

Match the part number on the old control, such as L8148E1299 or L4006E1125. If that number is discontinued, match the function (high limit, low limit or circulator), the temperature range and whether it needs a well.

Can I reuse the existing immersion well?

Usually, if the new control has the same bulb size and insertion depth. Add heat conductive grease to the well so the sensor reads the water temperature correctly.

Is a Resideo aquastat the same as a Honeywell aquastat?

Yes. Resideo makes the Honeywell Home aquastat line under the same model numbers. See all Resideo controls.

Related collections: boiler parts, low water cut-offs, temperature and pressure gauges and controls, switches and sensors.

collection.descriptionHtml:
A boiler fill valve, also called a boiler feed valve or pressure reducing valve, keeps a hydronic heating system at its cold-fill pressure. It adds make-up water automatically when the pressure drops. The collection lists fill and feed valves by part number: Caleffi AutoFill 553 series valves with or without a pressure gauge, Caleffi 573 and 574 COMBO models with a built-in backflow preventer, Resideo NK300S combination feed valves and the FM911 fill valve and backflow preventer assembly, and Taco 329 fast-fill and 335 boiler feed valves. The Caleffi F59650 replacement cartridge for the 553 series is listed as well.

If the boiler pressure keeps falling, the fill valve never shuts off or the relief valve drips, a worn or clogged fill valve is a common cause.

How to choose

  • Connection size and type: match the inlet and outlet, 1/2" or 3/4" on most models, in NPT, sweat, press or union.
  • Pressure setting: the valve must cover the cold-fill pressure of the system. Caleffi lists the AutoFill 553 as factory set at 15 psi and adjustable from 3 to 60 psi.
  • Backflow protection: many local codes require a backflow preventer on the boiler fill line. A combination valve saves space and two joints. Check whether your installation needs an ASSE 1012 or an ASSE 1013 device.
  • Pressure gauge: Caleffi 553642A and 553649A include a downstream gauge; other models are sold without one.

Common questions

What pressure should a boiler fill valve be set to?

Use the cold-fill pressure given for your system. Caleffi AutoFill 553 valves are factory set at 15 psi and adjust from 3 to 60 psi. Follow the boiler manufacturer instructions for your system.

Is a boiler fill valve the same as a boiler feed valve?

Yes. Fill valve, feed valve and pressure reducing valve are names for the same part on a hydronic heating system.

Do I need a backflow preventer on the fill line?

Many local codes require one. Combination models such as the Caleffi 573 COMBO and the Resideo FM911 put the fill valve and the backflow preventer in one assembly. See also backflow preventers.

Related collections: boiler parts, relief valves, heating expansion tanks, system fill tanks and Caleffi.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Air eliminators, air separators and hydraulic separators for hydronic heating systems. An air eliminator takes air out of the system water so it can be vented, and a hydraulic separator decouples the boiler loop from the system loop. The collection includes Resideo SuperVent air eliminators in NPT, sweat and press connections from 3/4" to 1-1/2", SuperVent replacement vent tops, Webstone press brass air separators from 3/4" to 1-1/2", the Taco 4900 series air separator and Taco air scoops, Legend Valve air and debris eliminators, Caleffi DISCAL DIRTMAG air and dirt separators with magnet, Caleffi hydro separators with sweat and press unions, and the Caleffi DiscalAir high discharge automatic air vent.

Install the air separator where the water is hottest and the pressure lowest, usually on the boiler supply ahead of the pump.

How to choose

  • Pipe size and flow: size the separator by pipe size and flow rate. Some titles list a Cv, such as 22 Cv on the 1" press SuperVent PV100P.
  • Connection: match NPT, sweat, press or union connections to the piping.
  • Function: choose an air eliminator, a combined air and dirt separator, or a hydraulic separator, depending on what the system needs.
  • Orientation: check whether the unit is for horizontal or vertical pipe; Webstone lists a separate 1" vertical model (H-78004-V).
  • Service parts: replacement vent tops are listed for Resideo SuperVent and Webstone air separators.

Common questions

Where should an air eliminator be installed?

Where the water is hottest and the pressure lowest, usually on the boiler supply ahead of the pump.

What is the difference between an air separator and a hydraulic separator?

An air separator removes air from the system water. A hydraulic separator decouples the boiler loop from the system loop so the flow in one does not disturb the other.

Can the vent top be replaced?

Yes, on some models. The Resideo PV-001RP and PV-020RP are replacement vent tops for SuperVent, and the Webstone H-74000 is a replacement vent assembly for 3/4" to 2" air separators.

Narrow it down: air separators, hydro separators, air and dirt separators, air vents and heating expansion tanks.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Hydronic expansion tanks and mounting hardware for closed-loop heating systems. The tank takes up the extra water volume as the system heats, which keeps the pressure below the relief valve setting. The collection includes Amtrol Extrol EX-15, EX-30 and EX-60 tanks, Zilmet ZHT tanks from 2.1 to 6.3 gallons and ZFT rectangular tanks, and Calefactio HGT tanks from 2.1 to 8 gallons, along with the Flamco 1/2" wall mount bracket and Axiom HN-2 and HN-3 wall bracket kits.

Heating tanks are not designed for potable water, so use a potable-rated thermal expansion tank on domestic water heaters.

How to choose

  • Tank volume: size the tank from the system water volume, the fill pressure, and the maximum operating temperature and pressure. Tanks here run from 2 to 8 gallons.
  • Precharge: set the tank precharge to match the system fill pressure before installing. Amtrol lists a 12 psig factory precharge on Extrol EX tanks.
  • Ratings: check the maximum working pressure and temperature of the tank against the system. Amtrol lists the Extrol EX at 100 psig and 240 °F.
  • Mounting: decide between hanging the tank from the piping and a wall bracket, and check the connection size in the product details.

Common questions

What size expansion tank do I need for my boiler?

Size it from the system water volume, the fill pressure and the maximum operating temperature and pressure. Manufacturer sizing tables use these inputs.

What should the precharge pressure be?

Set the precharge to match the system fill pressure before the tank is installed. Amtrol Extrol EX tanks are listed with a 12 psig factory precharge.

Can I use a heating expansion tank on a water heater?

No. Heating tanks are not designed for potable water. Use a tank from expansion tanks for water heating.

Related collections: expansion tanks for water heating, boiler fill valves, relief valves, air vents and boiler trim kits.

Manifolds and accessories for radiant floor heating. A manifold feeds supply water to each PEX loop and collects the return, and flow meters or balancing valves on the manifold let you set each loop. The collection includes MrPEX Systems 1-1/4" stainless steel manifold assemblies with flow meters and ball valves in up to 12 branches, MrPEX 1-1/2" chrome plated brass manifolds and composite manifold kits, Viega stainless steel heating and cooling manifolds, HeatLink 1-1/4" stainless steel manifolds with flow meters and PEX manifold tees, EK 20 and EK 25 loop adapters for 5/16" through 3/4" PEX, end caps, valve actuators, manifold cabinets and Caleffi manifold housing boxes.

Pressure test the loops before the floor is poured.

How to choose

  • Loop count: size the manifold by the number of loops. Assemblies here are listed with up to 12 branches.
  • Balancing: use models with flow meters or balancing valves where the loops differ in length.
  • Manifold and connection size: check the trunk size (1-1/4" or 1-1/2") and the supply and return connections, such as 1-1/4" x 1" union x FPT on Viega manifolds.
  • Loop adapters: match the EK 20 or EK 25 fitting assembly to the PEX size and type.
  • Actuators: actuators are listed as 2-wire or 4-wire. Confirm the actuator voltage against your zoning controls.

Common questions

How many loops can one manifold serve?

One loop per branch. Count the loops in the zone and pick a manifold with at least that many branches; assemblies here are listed with up to 12.

Do I need flow meters on a radiant manifold?

Use a manifold with flow meters or balancing valves where the loops differ in length, so each loop can be set.

What are EK 20 and EK 25 adapters?

They are MrPEX PEX fitting assemblies. Titles name the PEX size and the EK connection, for example 5/8" PEX to EK 25. Match the adapter to the manifold outlet and to the PEX size and type.

Related collections: radiant heating, PEX manifolds, oxygen barrier tubing, PEX pipe and radiant heating tools.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Taco Comfort Solutions circulators, zone valves and hydronic system parts. Pumps include 00 series cast iron circulators such as the 007 and the 0010 through 0015, with integral flow check options, ECM variable speed models such as the 007e, 0015e3, 0018e, 0026e and 0034e, stainless steel 006 and 007 circulators and Plumb N' Plug pumps with timers. Zoning parts include Zone Sentry, QuickTop and heat motor zone valves, SR500 series switching relays, ZVC400 series zone valve controls and the X-Pump Block. The collection also holds Hy-Vent air vents, the 4900 series air separator, 5000 series mixing valves, ACCU-FLO balancing valves, Freedom flange sets, replacement cartridges and 329 and 335 boiler feed valves.

Planning a zoned system? Try the Zone Planner.

How to choose

  • Flow and head: size a circulator to the flow and head the loop requires and compare them with the pump curve.
  • Body material: cast iron circulators suit closed heating loops. Use bronze or stainless steel bodies for open potable water systems.
  • Connections and voltage: confirm flanged, union or sweat connections and the supply voltage; most circulators here are listed at 115V/60/1.
  • Zone valves: match the pipe size, the sweat or press connection, normally closed or normally open action and the control voltage to your system.
  • Relays and controls: pick by the number of zones. SR switching relays are listed from 1 to 6 zones, with priority on multi-zone models.

Common questions

Taco 007 or 007e?

The 007 is the fixed-speed circulator, listed here in cast iron and stainless steel. The 007e is listed as a cast iron ECM high efficiency model. Compare the pump curves before swapping one for the other.

Which Taco zone valves are listed here?

Zone Sentry, QuickTop and heat motor zone valves. Match the pipe size, the connection, normally closed or normally open action and the control voltage. See Taco zone valves.

Can I replace only the cartridge in a Taco circulator?

Replacement cartridges are listed in Taco cartridges. Match the cartridge to the pump model.

Shop Taco by category: Taco circulator pumps, Taco zone valves, Taco cartridges, switching relays and air vents.

collection.descriptionHtml:
IBC boilers, indirect water heaters and service parts. The boilers are gas condensing models: SL G3 fire tube boilers from 85,000 to 260,000 BTU/h (SL 10-85, SL 14-115, SL 20-160, SL 30-199 and SL 26-260), VX series boilers at 110,000, 150,000 and 199,000 BTU/h, CX combi boilers at 150,000 and 199,000 BTU/h with 10:1 turndown, and SFC combi boilers from 125,000 to 199,000 BTU/h. Product titles list 94 to 96 percent efficiency and elevation ranges up to 10,000 or 12,000 feet. The collection also includes 444 stainless steel indirect water heaters from 26.8 to 119 gallons with aquastat, the SFT-199 tankless water heater, and replacement parts such as ignitor kits, fan kits, gas valve kits, sensors, control boards and parts kits.

For service parts, confirm the boiler model and series named in the part title.

How to choose

  • BTU input: size the boiler to a heat-loss calculation. Inputs here run from 85,000 to 260,000 BTU/h.
  • Heating only or combi: for CX and SFC combi units, check the domestic hot water flow as well as the heating output.
  • Pump: SL and VX titles list no pump included, and the SFC160-1 lists a built-in pump.
  • Elevation and fuel: SL titles list 0-12,000 ft and VX and SFC titles 0-10,000 ft. Check the gas type in the title before ordering.
  • Indirect tank: match the tank to the boiler output and to household hot water demand.

Common questions

IBC SL or VX series?

Both are fire tube condensing boilers listed at 95 to 96 percent efficiency. The SL G3 runs from 85,000 to 260,000 BTU/h with a listed elevation range up to 12,000 ft; the VX runs from 110,000 to 199,000 BTU/h with a range up to 10,000 ft. Compare the specifications of the two sizes you are considering.

Does an IBC boiler include a circulator?

It depends on the model. Titles state No Pump Included or Built-In Pump. If none is included, see circulator pumps.

How do I find the right IBC part?

Part titles name the series they fit, such as SL G1/G2/G3, VX, HC/DC or SFT and SFC. Confirm the boiler model and series before ordering.

Related collections: IBC parts, condensing boilers, combi boilers, indirect water heaters and condensate neutralizers.
