collection.descriptionHtml:
Line voltage thermostats switch electric baseboard heaters, convectors, fan-forced heaters and floor heating directly at 120, 208 or 240 V, with no transformer or relay in between. They are not interchangeable with 24 V thermostats. The models here are Honeywell Home and Resideo.

The T410 and T498 are electric heat thermostats for baseboard heaters. Some T498 models have been discontinued by the manufacturer; each product page shows its status. Electronic models include the TL7235 non-programmable double-pole thermostat for 208/240 V, the TL8130 single-pole and TL8230 double-pole 7-day programmable thermostats, the TH114 manual and TH115 7-day programmable series, and the TH401 and TH450 manual thermostats with TRIAC switching. For electric floor heating, the TH115-AF-GA is a 7-day programmable floor thermostat for 120/240 V, rated 15 A, with a 5 mA GFCI.

How to choose

  • Supply voltage: check the voltage of the heater circuit. The TH401 and TH450 are listed for 120, 208 and 240 V, while the TL7235, TL8130 and TL8230 are listed for 208 and 240 V.
  • Single-pole or double-pole: a double-pole (DPST) thermostat breaks both legs of a 240 V circuit and gives a true off position. A single-pole (SPST) model breaks one leg, so the heater stays connected to power when the thermostat is off.
  • Load: add up the wattage of every heater on the thermostat and compare it with the thermostat's rating at your voltage. The TL7235 and TL8230 are listed at 15 A maximum, which is 3,600 W at 240 V.
  • Heater type: the specifications list the heaters each model is made for. The TL7235, TL8130 and TL8230 list electric baseboards, convectors and fan-forced heaters (resistive loads). Floor heating needs a floor heating thermostat such as the TH115-AF-GA.
  • Manual or programmable: manual models hold one setpoint; the TH115, TL8130 and TL8230 run 7-day schedules.

Common questions

What is a line voltage thermostat?

It switches a 120 V or 240 V electric heater directly, with no transformer. It is used for electric baseboard, convectors, fan-forced wall heaters and electric floor heat.

Single-pole or double-pole: which do I need?

A double-pole thermostat breaks both legs of a 240 V circuit and gives a true off position; a single-pole thermostat breaks one leg. Replace the old thermostat with the same type, and follow the manufacturer instructions and local electrical code.

Can I use a 24 V or smart thermostat on baseboard heat?

Not directly. A 24 V thermostat needs an electric heat relay with a transformer between it and the heater; see relays.

Related: non-programmable thermostats and programmable thermostats for 24 V systems, thermostat accessories, baseboard heaters and all thermostats.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Accessories for Honeywell Home and Resideo thermostats. Cover plates hide the paint line and screw holes left when a smaller thermostat replaces a larger one; they are made for a specific series, such as the 50002883-001 for FocusPRO and PRO models, the 50022893-001 for PRO TH1000 and TH2000 thermostats and the THP2400A1019 for the RedLINK VisionPRO.

TG511 medium and TG512 large universal thermostat guards are locking covers that stop tampering in public and commercial spaces; 191990A replacement keys fit the TG509 to TG512 guards. The THP9045A1023 WireSaver is a C-wire adapter for Wi-Fi thermostats and RedLINK 8000 series models. Remote sensors include the C7189U1005 indoor temperature sensor and the C7089U1006 outdoor temperature sensor.

How to choose

  • Thermostat series: cover plates and wall plates fit one series. Match the series named in the product title to the model number on the back of the thermostat body.
  • Plate size: measure the mark on the wall. The plate has to be larger than the old thermostat's outline; sizes are in the titles, for example 7-7/8 x 5-1/2 in for the 32003796-001.
  • Guard size: a guard must clear the thermostat on all sides and in depth. TG511 is the medium size and TG512 the large; clear versions let the display be read.
  • Sensor compatibility: a remote sensor works only with thermostats that have a sensor input for it. Check the thermostat's installation guide for the sensor part number it accepts.
  • C-wire adapter: the WireSaver is listed for Wi-Fi thermostats and RedLINK 8000 series models. Confirm that the thermostat and equipment are covered before ordering.

Common questions

Which cover plate fits my thermostat?

Cover plates are made for a thermostat series, so match the series in the product title, such as PRO, FocusPRO, VisionPRO or Prestige. Several T6 Pro thermostats are listed with a small decorative cover plate included.

What if my wall has no C-wire?

A C-wire adapter such as the THP9045A1023 WireSaver adds a common at the equipment so a Wi-Fi thermostat can be powered without pulling new cable. The other option is new thermostat wire with a spare conductor.

What is a thermostat guard for?

It is a locking cover that goes over the thermostat so that only someone with the key can change the setting. Guards are common in offices, schools, rentals and shared spaces.

Related: programmable thermostats, non-programmable thermostats, RedLINK accessories, thermostat wire and all thermostats.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Honeywell Home Pro Series thermostats are made by Resideo for the HVAC trade. This collection groups the T6 Pro family with the PRO 1000, PRO 2000, PRO 3000, T1 Pro, T3 Pro and T4 Pro models so they can be compared in one place.

In the T6 Pro line, the TH6210U2001 covers up to 2 heat/1 cool heat pumps or 1 heat/1 cool conventional systems, the TH6220U2000 up to 2 heat/2 cool conventional, and the TH6320U2008 up to 3 heat/2 cool heat pumps or 2 heat/2 cool conventional. The family also has a hydronic heat-only version with a floor sensor (TH6100AF2004), a Wi-Fi version (T6 Pro Smart TH6220WF2006) and a Z-Wave version. Some models in the PRO 1000, PRO 2000, PRO 3000, T1 Pro, T3 Pro and T4 Pro lines have been discontinued by the manufacturer; each product page shows its status and replacement.

How to choose

  • Conventional or heat pump: note whether the system is a furnace with an air conditioner or a heat pump.
  • Stages: count the heating and cooling stages and choose a model that covers them. "2 Heat/1 Cool heat pump" means one compressor stage plus auxiliary heat.
  • Programmable or not: T6 Pro and PRO 2000 models run a schedule; PRO 1000 models are non-programmable. The PRO 2000 specifications list a 5-2 day program.
  • C-wire: the T6 Pro Smart Wi-Fi version is listed as hardwired, so check for a common (C) wire at the wall before ordering.
  • Horizontal or vertical: PRO 1000 and PRO 2000 part numbers with DH are horizontal and with DV are vertical. T6 Pro models mount on the UWP wall plate.

Common questions

Which Honeywell Pro Series thermostats are discontinued?

Some models in the PRO 1000, PRO 2000, PRO 3000, T1 Pro, T3 Pro and T4 Pro lines have been discontinued by the manufacturer. Each product page shows the status of that model and its replacement. For older part numbers, see the Honeywell to Resideo cross-reference.

Which Pro thermostat do I need for a heat pump?

Pick a model whose heat pump stage rating covers the system. The T6 Pro TH6210U2001 and TH6220U2000 handle up to 2 heat/1 cool heat pumps and the TH6320U2008 up to 3 heat/2 cool. The PRO 1000 TH1210DV1007 is a non-programmable 2 heat/1 cool heat pump model.

Is there a Wi-Fi Pro thermostat?

Yes. The T6 Pro Smart TH6220WF2006 is the Wi-Fi version, listed for up to 2 heat/1 cool heat pumps or 2 heat/2 cool conventional systems. See smart thermostats for other connected models.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Zone dampers split one forced-air heating and cooling system into zones, each with its own thermostat. A damper in each branch or trunk duct opens and closes on command from a zone control panel. The dampers here are Honeywell Home TrueZONE models made by Resideo, in four types.

ZD dampers are rectangular parallel blade dampers sized width by height in inches, such as the ZD10X12TZ for a 10 x 12 in duct. ARD dampers are round automatic dampers, listed as normally open, in sizes from 5 in to 20 in. RRD retrofit round dampers come in 5 in to 8 in sizes. EARD dampers are 6 in and 8 in round fresh air dampers for a ventilation intake. A zoned system also needs a zone panel, a thermostat for each zone and a way to relieve static pressure when only a small zone is calling.

How to choose

  • Duct shape and size: for rectangular duct, measure the inside width and height and order that ZD size so the damper fits without transitions. For round duct, order the ARD by duct diameter.
  • Damper type: ZD and ARD dampers are zone dampers. EARD dampers are for a fresh air intake, not for zoning a supply branch.
  • Bypass: when one small zone calls, the blower still moves air for the whole system. A bypass damper relieves the extra static pressure and is sized together with the zone dampers, not afterward.
  • Zone panel: the number of dampers and zones has to match what the panel can control. TrueZONE HZ311 and HZ322 panels control 3 zones and the HZ432 controls 4.

Common questions

How do I size a rectangular zone damper?

Measure the inside width and height of the duct and order that size. The part number gives the dimensions: a ZD10X20TZ fits a 10 x 20 in duct.

Do I need a bypass damper?

Often, yes. When a small zone calls on its own, the blower still moves air for the whole house, and a bypass damper relieves that extra static pressure. Size it together with the zone dampers.

Can I replace just the damper motor?

Replacement damper actuators, such as the Honeywell Home M847D-ZONE two-position spring-open actuator, are listed in replacement actuators. Check the actuator's product page for the dampers it fits.

Related: forced air zone panels, bypass dampers, replacement actuators, transformers and thermostats.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Zone control panels for forced-air heating and cooling. The panel takes the calls from each zone thermostat, opens and closes the zone dampers and runs the furnace, air conditioner or heat pump. The panels here are Honeywell Home TrueZONE models made by Resideo.

The HZ311 controls 3 zones of 1 heat/1 cool equipment and is not heat pump compatible. The HZ322 controls 3 zones with up to 2 heat/2 cool stages and is heat pump compatible. The HZ432 controls 4 zones with up to 3 heat/2 cool stages, is heat pump compatible and expands to 32 zones with TAZ-4H Add-A-Zone panels, which add 4 zones each. The HZ221 is a 2-zone panel. Part numbers ending in K are kits that add an AT140 transformer and a C7735A discharge air temperature sensor to the panel.

How to choose

  • Number of zones: count the zones now and any planned later. Only the HZ432 expands, in steps of 4 zones with TAZ-4H panels.
  • Equipment stages: match the panel to the heating and cooling stages of the equipment: 1 heat/1 cool for the HZ311, up to 2 heat/2 cool for the HZ322 and up to 3 heat/2 cool for the HZ432.
  • Conventional or heat pump: a heat pump needs an HZ322 or HZ432, which also have an emergency heat switch. The HZ311 is for conventional equipment only.
  • Panel or kit: the kit includes the transformer and the discharge air temperature sensor. Order the panel alone only if both are already on hand.
  • Thermostats: each zone needs its own thermostat. RedLINK wireless thermostats connect to an HZ322 or HZ432 through the THM4000R1000 wireless adapter.

Common questions

Panel or kit: what is the difference?

The kit versions, such as the HZ311K, HZ322K and HZ432K, add an AT140 transformer and a C7735A discharge air temperature sensor to the panel.

Which TrueZONE panel works with a heat pump?

The HZ322 and HZ432 are listed as heat pump compatible, with up to 2 heat/2 cool and 3 heat/2 cool stages. The HZ311 is not heat pump compatible.

What else does a zoned system need?

Each zone needs a thermostat and a motorized zone damper, and most systems need a bypass damper or another way to relieve static pressure when few zones are calling.

Related: zone dampers, bypass dampers, Honeywell RedLINK thermostats, transformers and thermostats.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Whole-house humidifiers, dehumidifiers and their replacement parts, from Honeywell Home (made by Resideo). Humidifiers come in three types. Bypass models, such as the HE100, HE150, HE200 and HE250, use furnace airflow across an evaporator pad and need a bypass duct. Fan-powered models carry their own fan and need no bypass duct: the HE300 is listed at 18 gallons per day and includes a HumidiPRO digital humidity control. Steam models, such as the HM750 electrode humidifier, make steam in a replaceable cylinder.

Whole-home dehumidifiers come in 65, 90 and 120 pint per day sizes. Most of the collection is parts listed by the models they fit: HC22 and HC26 evaporator pads, solenoid valves, circuit boards, HM700 and HM750 steam cylinders, and filters for the DR65, DR90 and DR120 dehumidifiers.

How to choose

  • Humidifier type: a bypass model needs room for a bypass duct between supply and return. A fan-powered model mounts without one.
  • Capacity: compare the gallons per day rating with the size and air-tightness of the house. The HE300 is listed at 18 gallons per day and the HM750 replacement cylinder for 11 or 22 gallons per day.
  • Pad by model: the HC22 pad is for the HE220 and HE225. The HC26 pad is for the HE200, HE250, HE260, HE265, HE300, HE360 and HE365. Read the model number on the humidifier label.
  • Control: the H6062 HumidiPRO is a 24 Vac digital humidity control with an outdoor sensor, for return duct or wall mounting.
  • Dehumidifier filters: the 50049537-005 filter is for the DR65; the 50070171-002 filter is for the DR90A2000 and DR120A2000.

Common questions

Which humidifier pad do I need?

Find the model number on the humidifier. HE220 and HE225 units take an HC22 pad. HE200, HE250, HE260, HE265, HE300, HE360 and HE365 units take an HC26 pad.

How often should a humidifier pad be replaced?

The pad is a consumable. Minerals in the water scale it up over time. Follow the replacement interval in the humidifier manual.

Bypass, fan-powered or steam?

Bypass humidifiers rely on furnace airflow and a bypass duct. Fan-powered humidifiers have their own fan. Steam humidifiers make steam in a cylinder. The whole-house humidifier guide covers sizing.

Related: whole-house dehumidifiers, air cleaners and filters, indoor air quality, ERV and HRV ventilators and all Honeywell Home.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Whole-house air cleaners, replacement media filters and parts, from Honeywell Home (made by Resideo). A media air cleaner is a cabinet at the return duct that holds a deep pleated filter. The F100 media air cleaner is listed at MERV 11 in 16 x 20, 16 x 25, 20 x 20 and 20 x 25 in sizes.

Replacement media includes FC100 filters, which are MERV 11 in most sizes, FC200 charged-media filters at MERV 13, POPUP filters for the cabinets named in each title, and the FC40R return grille filter. Electronic air cleaners, such as the F300, charge particles and collect them on cells that are washed and reused; prefilters and postfilters for the F50 and F300 are sold as parts. The collection also has replacement lamps for the UV100 and UV2400 ultraviolet air treatment systems.

How to choose

  • Cabinet model and face size: media filters are sized to the cabinet, not to the duct. Match the part number on the old filter or the cabinet model, then the face size, such as 16 x 25 or 20 x 25 in.
  • MERV rating: FC100 media is listed at MERV 11 in most sizes and FC200 charged media at MERV 13. A higher MERV filter catches finer particles and adds resistance to airflow.
  • Media or electronic: a media cleaner uses a filter that is thrown away. An electronic cleaner uses collector cells that are washed, plus prefilters and postfilters matched to the model.
  • Space at the return: adding a media cabinet needs room at the return plenum next to the furnace or air handler. Check that before choosing a size.
  • UV lamps: order the lamp by the system it fits: the UC100E1006 is an 18 W lamp for the UV100E and the UV2400XLAM1 is the lamp for the UV2400.

Common questions

Which replacement filter fits my cabinet?

Match the part number printed on the old filter or the cabinet model, such as F100 or F200, and the face size. For example, the FC100A1037 is a 20 x 25 in MERV 11 replacement media filter.

How often should a media filter be replaced?

Follow the cabinet manual, and replace the filter sooner if airflow drops or the media looks loaded.

MERV 11 or MERV 13?

FC100 media is listed at MERV 11 in most sizes and FC200 charged media at MERV 13. A higher rating catches smaller particles and adds resistance to airflow; when in doubt, stay with the rating the cabinet was supplied with.

Related: humidifiers and dehumidifiers, indoor air quality, ERV and HRV ventilators and all Honeywell Home.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Ignition and flame-sensing parts for gas furnaces, boilers and water heaters, mostly Resideo (formerly Honeywell) with DiversiTech and Rheem. Hot surface igniters include the Q4100 silicon carbide series, which differ by lead length and mounting, and the Q3200U1004 GLOWFLY, a one-piece 120 Vac multisystem igniter. Flame sensors include the Resideo Q354A1018 and DiversiTech sensors listed by the Goodman, Lennox and Trane parts they replace.

Pilot burners cover standing pilot (Q314, Q327), intermittent pilot (Q345, Q348) and SmartValve pilot hardware (Q3450 pilot burners and Q3400 igniter flame rod assemblies). Ignition controls include the S8910U universal hot surface ignition module and the Y8610U intermittent pilot retrofit kit. Ignition cables, pilot orifices and compression fittings for pilot tubing complete the collection.

How to choose

  • Original part number: start with the number on the old part or in the appliance manual, then match it or use a published cross-reference. Universal parts list the systems they cover.
  • Igniter: match the voltage, the lead length and the mounting. Q4100 igniters are listed with lead lengths from 5 in to 19-1/8 in.
  • Pilot burner: match the gas type, the orifice (for example BCR-18 for natural gas), the tip direction (left, right or front) and the mounting bracket style.
  • Flame sensor: match the rod shape, the angle and the bracket. DiversiTech sensors name the furnace brand part numbers they replace in the title.
  • Ignition control: match the ignition type (direct spark, hot surface or intermittent pilot), one-rod or two-rod flame sensing, and the trial and lockout timing given in the specifications.

Common questions

How do I pick a replacement hot surface igniter?

Use the part number on the old igniter or in the furnace manual. If that number is not listed, compare voltage, lead length, connector and mounting bracket. The Q3200U1004 is a multisystem 120 Vac igniter; check its list of covered models first.

Should I clean or replace a flame sensor?

A flame sensor rod with a light coating can often be cleaned gently and put back. Replace it if the rod is bent, pitted or the ceramic is cracked. The steps are in the guide to cleaning, testing and replacing a furnace ignitor and flame sensor.

What should I check on a pilot burner?

Match the gas type, the orifice size, the tip direction and the bracket style to the burner being replaced, and check whether it is for a standing pilot, an intermittent pilot or a SmartValve system. Gas appliance repairs should be done by a qualified technician.

Related: gas valves, thermocouples and thermopiles, pilot, burner and ignition parts, fan and limit controllers and all Resideo controls.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Combination gas valves for furnaces, boilers and water heaters, made by Resideo (formerly Honeywell). A gas valve is matched to the ignition system of the appliance. Standing pilot valves (VR8200, VR8300 and the 120 V VR4300) keep a pilot lit at all times. Intermittent pilot valves (VR8204, VR8304) light the pilot on each call for heat. Direct ignition valves (VR8205, VR8215, VR8305 and the two-stage VR9205) light the main burner from a hot surface or spark igniter, with no pilot. Universal valves (VR8245, VR8345) are listed for both intermittent pilot and direct ignition.

SmartValve controls (SV9501, SV9510, SV9541, SV9601, SV9641) combine the gas valve and the ignition control in one body. Water heater gas valves (WT8840) are listed by the water heater they fit. Conversion kits change the regulator between natural gas and LP.

How to choose

  • Ignition type: standing pilot, intermittent pilot, direct ignition or SmartValve. The valve and the ignition control have to match.
  • Inlet and outlet size: 1/2 x 1/2 in, 1/2 x 3/4 in or 3/4 x 3/4 in. Some valves include reducer bushings or a straight flange; the specifications list what is in the box.
  • Capacity: compare the valve capacity with the appliance input. The VR8205A2024 is listed at 150,000 Btu/h and the VR8345M4302 at 300,000 Btu/h, both at 1 in. wc pressure drop.
  • Opening and stages: standard, slow, step or fast opening, and single-stage or two-stage. Use the same characteristic as the original valve.
  • Gas type: titles give the factory setting, such as 3.5 in. wc for natural gas. Many valves include a natural to LP conversion kit; kits are also listed separately for single-stage and two-stage valves.

Common questions

How do I find the right replacement gas valve?

Read the model number on the old valve, for example VR8205A2024 or VR8345M4302, and order the same number. If it is no longer made, match the ignition type, voltage, pipe sizes, capacity, opening type and number of stages. The guide to furnace gas valve replacement walks through each one.

Can a natural gas valve be converted to LP?

Many VR8200 and VR8300 series valves take a regulator conversion kit, and several include a natural to LP kit in the box. Kits differ for single-stage and two-stage valves, for example the 396221 and the 396021. A conversion must be done by a qualified gas technician.

Are Honeywell and Resideo gas valves the same?

Yes. Resideo makes the former Honeywell gas valve line under the same model numbers. For older part numbers, see the Honeywell to Resideo cross-reference.

Related: igniters, flame sensors and pilot burners, thermocouples and thermopiles, pilot, burner and ignition parts, fan and limit controllers and all Resideo controls.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Control transformers that step line voltage down to 24 V for thermostats, zone panels, gas valves, relays and contactor coils. The models here are Resideo (formerly Honeywell) AT series transformers.

Each product's specifications give its output in VA. Primary voltages include 120 V, 120/208/240 V, 277 V, 208/277/480 V and 480 V. Mounting styles include foot mount, plate mount, clamp mount, panel mount and multi-mount models that cover several of these. The AT150F and AT175F have a circuit breaker with a manual reset button, and AT88 models are listed with a fused secondary. Many models are listed with 9 in leadwires.

How to choose

  • Primary voltage: match the supply: 120 V, 208/240 V, 277 V or 480 V. Multi-tap models such as the AT140B1214 cover 120, 208 and 240 V.
  • VA rating: add up the load of every 24 V device on the circuit and leave some margin. For zone panels, follow the panel instructions.
  • Mounting: foot mount for a panel or furnace cabinet, plate mount for a junction box, or a multi-mount model when the mounting is not known in advance.
  • Protection: choose a model with a manual reset circuit breaker or a fused secondary where a short in field wiring is a risk.

Common questions

What size (VA) transformer do I need?

Add the VA or the current draw of everything the transformer powers: thermostat, relays, gas valve, zone valves or dampers. Choose a rating above that total.

How do I match a replacement transformer?

Read the label on the old one for primary voltage, secondary voltage and VA, then note how it is mounted and whether it has leadwires or screw terminals. The part number on the label, such as AT140A1000, can be ordered directly.

Related: relays, contactors, forced air zone panels, zone dampers and thermostats.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Relays for HVAC and hydronic controls, mostly Resideo (formerly Honeywell) with Functional Devices and DiversiTech. General purpose relays switch fans, pumps and other loads from a control circuit: the R8222 has a 24 Vac coil with SPDT or DPDT contacts, and the R4222 has a 120 V or 208/240 V coil.

Switching relays with an internal transformer, such as the RA832A, the R845A and the R8845U multisystem model, let a 24 V thermostat switch a line voltage device such as a burner or circulator. Electric heat relays (R841, RC840) let a low voltage thermostat control a line voltage resistive load such as baseboard or duct heaters; RC840T models include a transformer for a given supply voltage. The collection also has DiversiTech heat sequencers, the Functional Devices RIBU1C pilot relay, fan centers and defrost controls.

How to choose

  • Coil voltage: the coil has to match the control circuit: 24 Vac from a thermostat circuit, or 120 V or 208/240 V for a line voltage control.
  • Contact arrangement: SPST, SPDT, DPST or DPDT. Match the original, or count the circuits that must be made and broken.
  • Contact rating: check the load against the rating for its type. Ratings differ for resistive loads and for motors: the R8222D1014 is listed at 12 A full load and 20.8 A resistive at 120 Vac.
  • Transformer: a relay with an internal transformer supplies its own 24 V for the thermostat circuit. A relay without one needs 24 V from another source.
  • Supply voltage: for RC840T electric heat relays, pick the version for the heater supply, such as RC840T-120 or RC840T-240.

Common questions

What is a switching relay used for?

It lets a 24 V thermostat or control switch a line voltage load such as a circulator pump, fan or burner. Models with an internal transformer also power the thermostat circuit.

Which relay lets a 24 V thermostat control baseboard heat?

An electric heat relay such as the RC840 or R841. The RC840T-120 and RC840T-240 include a transformer, so they supply the 24 V control power themselves. Check the relay rating against the heater load.

What is the R8845U1003 multisystem relay?

It is a universal switching relay with an internal transformer, for 24 V two-wire or three-wire thermostat control of line voltage devices. For older Honeywell relay numbers, see the Honeywell to Resideo cross-reference.

Related: switching relays for hydronic zoning, contactors, transformers and line voltage thermostats.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Definite purpose contactors for air conditioner and heat pump condensing units, electric heat and other HVAC loads, made by Resideo (formerly Honeywell). A contactor is the heavy-duty relay that switches the compressor and fan motor when the thermostat calls. Three things define one: the number of poles, the full load amp rating and the coil voltage (24, 120, 208/240 or 277 Vac).

Product titles and specifications give the poles, the amp ratings and the coil voltage of each model. Some DP series models have been discontinued by the manufacturer; each product page shows its status. The DPL series is marked A2L compliant, for equipment that uses A2L refrigerants such as R-454B and R-32. The Rheem SP12841 is a 3-pole contactor assembly for water heaters.

How to choose

  • Poles: match the pole count of the original contactor: 1, 2 or 3 poles in most equipment, with 4-pole models also listed.
  • Amp rating: the replacement must match or exceed the original full load amp rating. Full load and resistive ratings differ: one 3-pole 40 A model is listed at 40 A full load and 50 A resistive.
  • Coil voltage: the coil must match the control circuit exactly. A 24 Vac coil is used when the thermostat circuit pulls the contactor in; 120, 208/240 and 277 Vac coils are for line voltage control.
  • Refrigerant: for equipment that uses an A2L refrigerant, choose a contactor marked A2L compliant, such as the DPL series.

Common questions

How do I match a replacement contactor?

Read the label on the old one for poles, full load amps (FLA) and coil voltage. The replacement should match the poles and coil voltage and match or exceed the amp rating. Check that the terminals suit the existing wiring.

The DP contactor I need is discontinued. What do I order?

Some DP series part numbers have been discontinued by the manufacturer, and the product page shows the status. Order by specification: the same number of poles, the same coil voltage and an equal or higher amp rating.

Related: relays, transformers, thermostats and all HVAC parts.

Resideo controls and replacement parts for heating, cooling and hydronic systems. Resideo was spun off from Honeywell in 2018 and makes the Honeywell Home line, so a part number from an older Honeywell manual usually identifies a current Resideo part.

The catalog here covers thermostats, gas valves, ignition controls and pilot burners, aquastats and wells, zone valves and actuators, switching relays, transformers, contactors, fan and limit controls, zone dampers and panels, air cleaners and humidifier parts. Most of these are model-specific replacement parts: order by the number printed on the old part or on the appliance data plate, not by the appliance description. The Honeywell to Resideo cross-reference indexes the Honeywell series, including L, V, VR, Q, ZD and TH numbers, and shows where each sits in the catalog.

How to choose

  • Thermostats: check the voltage first: 24 V for gas, heat pump and hydronic equipment, line voltage for electric baseboard. Some models in the PRO, T-Series and FocusPRO lines have been discontinued by the manufacturer; each product page shows its status and replacement. See thermostats and line voltage thermostats.

Common questions

Is Resideo the same company as Honeywell Home?

Resideo was spun off from Honeywell in 2018 and makes and supports the Honeywell Home product line. Many part numbers are sold under both names, so an older Honeywell number usually identifies a current Resideo part.

How do I find the Resideo part for an old Honeywell number?

Search the store for the number without its suffix, for example VR8205. If it is not listed, the Honeywell to Resideo cross-reference shows where that series sits in the catalog.

Are discontinued Honeywell thermostats still listed?

Some models in the PRO 1000, PRO 2000 and PRO 3000, T1 Pro, T3 Pro and T4 Pro and FocusPRO 5000 and 6000 lines have been discontinued by the manufacturer. Each product page shows its status and replacement. See Honeywell Pro Series thermostats.

collection.descriptionHtml:
Honeywell Home is the brand on thermostats, zoning and indoor air quality products made and supported by Resideo, so many part numbers are sold under both names. This collection holds Honeywell Home thermostats, TrueZONE zone panels and dampers, VC zone valves, media air cleaners and filters, humidifiers, dehumidifiers and the replacement parts for them.

By category: TrueZONE zone dampers · Bypass dampers · Zone valves (2-way, 3-way, fan coil) · Zone valve replacement heads · Zone valve parts · Thermostats (smart, programmable, non-programmable) · Thermostat accessories · RedLINK accessories · Air cleaners & filters · Humidifiers & dehumidifiers · ERV/HRV ventilation · Radiator valves · Leak detection

Thermostat lines include the T6 Pro, the FocusPRO N100, P200 and S200, the VisionPRO 8000 with RedLINK, the PRO 1000, 2000 and 3000, the T1 Pro, T3 Pro and T4 Pro, the FocusPRO 5000 and 6000 and the T10 Pro. Some models in these lines have been discontinued by the manufacturer; each product page shows its status and replacement. If an older manual gives a Honeywell number that is not listed, check the Honeywell to Resideo cross-reference.

How to choose

  • Thermostats: choose by voltage (24 V or line voltage), by system type (conventional or heat pump), by heat and cool stages and by schedule. Wi-Fi models need a C-wire. See thermostats, smart thermostats and line voltage thermostats.
  • Forced-air zoning: a TrueZONE system uses a zone panel, a damper in each zone duct and usually a bypass damper. Rectangular dampers are sized by duct width and height. See zone panels, zone dampers and bypass dampers.
  • Hydronic zoning: VC zone valves have a separate valve body and actuator, so a failed head can be replaced without draining the loop. Choose the body by pipe size and Cv, then the actuator by voltage and control type. See zone valves.
  • Indoor air quality: filters, pads and lamps are matched to the model number of the air cleaner, humidifier or UV system. See air cleaners and filters and humidifiers and dehumidifiers.
  • Wireless accessories: RedLINK sensors and modules work only with RedLINK thermostats. See RedLINK accessories.

Common questions

Are Honeywell Home and Resideo the same?

Resideo makes and supports the Honeywell Home line. Many part numbers carry a Resideo prefix in catalogs while the product itself is sold as Honeywell Home.

My Honeywell thermostat is discontinued. What replaces it?

Match the system type, the stages and the schedule type of the old model. The product page of a discontinued model shows its replacement. For older part numbers, see the Honeywell to Resideo cross-reference.

Where are all the Honeywell Home thermostats?

In the thermostats collection, which is split into non-programmable, programmable, smart and line voltage models.

See also all Resideo controls.
